title: COVID-19 Higher Mortality in Chinese Regions With Chronic Exposure to Lower Air Quality.
outcome_retrieval_evidence: Direct raw GitHub CSV route is specified and publicly downloadable.
outcome_variable_evidence: CSV supplies prefecture-level confirmed cases, deaths, and population-derived mortality measures.
date_key_evidence: Filename and paper define the 2020-05-23 outcome snapshot.
covariate_evidence: Released file contains reported demographic/health and pollution covariates used for the ecological model.
analysis_specification_evidence: Paper defines the regional ecological regression and adjustment set.
aeris_exposure_evidence: AERIS can independently construct city-level ambient criteria-pollutant summaries from public monitoring data; historical source/monitor selection must be pinned.
implementation_requirements: No blocker; historical exposure reconstruction requires a documented city aggregation adapter.

title: Association of air pollution and weather conditions during infection course with COVID-19 case fatality rate in the United Kingdom.
outcome_retrieval_evidence: GOV.UK provides a public CSV download pathway for UK COVID cases and deaths.
outcome_variable_evidence: Paper defines daily COVID case-fatality rate from confirmed cases and deaths.
date_key_evidence: Study period is 2020-03-26 through 2020-09-15 with daily observations.
covariate_evidence: Primary model specifies weather factors and time-varying epidemiological terms.
analysis_specification_evidence: Paper specifies a GLMM combined with distributed-lag nonlinear models and infection-stage lags.
aeris_exposure_evidence: AERIS-compatible public monitors can support country/day exposure aggregation; monitor and spatial aggregation adapter must be documented.
implementation_requirements: No outcome-data blocker; exposure and endpoint transformation need implementation adapters.

title: Inequities in air pollution on stroke mortality among Older Americans: a U.S. nationwide analysis.
outcome_retrieval_evidence: CDC WONDER and the CDC Interactive Atlas are public query systems, but the county/age/cause query must be reproduced and exported.
outcome_variable_evidence: Paper defines annual county ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke mortality rates among adults 65+ per 100,000.
geography_key_evidence: Methods identify county/county-equivalent units and exclusions.
covariate_evidence: Methods enumerate CDC Atlas risk factors and ACS income, poverty, Gini, insurance, and park-access covariates; source-query joins are required.
analysis_specification_evidence: Paper gives the multivariable linear equation, logistic model, variables, and subgroup definitions.
aeris_exposure_evidence: AERIS can independently build county annual PM2.5 summaries from public monitoring data, requiring a county aggregation and monitor-coverage adapter.
implementation_requirements: Public multi-source queries and county aggregation require explicit adapters.

title: Effects of the spread of COVID-19 on public health of polluted cities: results of the first wave for explaining the dejà vu in the second wave of COVID-19 pandemic and epidemics of future vital agents.
outcome_retrieval_evidence: Mendeley Data record exposes a CC-BY dataset and Download All pathway without account login.
outcome_variable_evidence: Repository description identifies COVID diffusion/outcome measures among the released Italian city factors.
date_key_evidence: Paper fixes the first-wave Italian analysis period.
geography_key_evidence: Released dataset is organized by Italian city.
covariate_evidence: Dataset description names demographic, respiratory, wind, and pollution factors used in analysis.
analysis_specification_evidence: Paper provides the first-wave ecological analysis definition.
aeris_exposure_evidence: AERIS can reconstruct city-level ambient pollutant summaries from public monitoring data with a documented city/monitor aggregation adapter.
implementation_requirements: No access blocker; release workbook and exposure aggregation must be normalized.

title: Effects of chronic exposure to ambient air pollutants on COVID-19 morbidity and mortality - A lesson from OECD countries.
outcome_retrieval_evidence: Official WHO global COVID CSV is a direct unauthenticated download.
outcome_variable_evidence: CSV contains country-date confirmed cases and deaths; paper defines derived morbidity and mortality measures.
date_key_evidence: Methods define 2020-01-21 to 2020-06-07 and event-time days since first case.
covariate_evidence: Paper names World Bank and OECD public indicators; country-year extraction and joins are required.
analysis_specification_evidence: Methods specify correlations and multivariable regressions at prespecified event times.
aeris_exposure_evidence: Country-level monitoring reconstruction is feasible in principle using AERIS-compatible public monitors, but needs documented coverage and population/country aggregation.
implementation_requirements: Exposure substitution and public covariate adapters are required.

title: Effects of chronic exposure to ambient air pollutants, demographic, and socioeconomic factors on COVID-19 morbidity: The Israeli case study.
outcome_retrieval_evidence: Israeli government CSV route is a concrete unauthenticated municipality-level download.
outcome_variable_evidence: Paper uses municipal COVID morbidity/case outcomes from the government table.
date_key_evidence: Methods define the study period and cumulative municipal outcome timing.
geography_key_evidence: Government CSV and paper use municipality identifiers.
covariate_evidence: Paper identifies official demographic and socioeconomic municipal sources; joins require a source adapter.
analysis_specification_evidence: Paper supplies a bounded municipal regression specification and covariate set.
aeris_exposure_evidence: AERIS can independently construct municipality-level ambient criteria-pollution summaries from public monitoring data with a documented assignment adapter.
implementation_requirements: No outcome-access blocker; covariate joins and municipality-monitor assignment require adapters.

title: Impact of long-term exposure to PM2.5 and temperature on coronavirus disease mortality: observed trends in France.
outcome_retrieval_evidence: Paper-reported data.gouv resource is a direct public file endpoint; the dataset page documents department-level daily hospital COVID indicators and CSV downloads without login: https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/donnees-hospitalieres-relatives-a-lepidemie-de-covid-19
outcome_variable_evidence: Outcome is cumulative hospital COVID-19 deaths per 100,000 residents at department level.
date_key_evidence: Article evaluates cumulative mortality snapshots from 1 May through 31 December 2020; the public outcome files have daily department date keys.
geography_key_evidence: Study includes 96 mainland-France departments (NUTS 3); department code is the join key.
covariate_evidence: Table 1 enumerates public covariates: intensive/resuscitation beds, physician density, age 60+, male share, unemployment, urban population, diabetes, cancer, chronic respiratory disease, and obesity.
analysis_specification_evidence: Negative-binomial department-level mortality-rate models use PM2.5 quartiles and temperature with the listed confounders at specified monthly/end-December snapshots.
aeris_exposure_evidence: Paper used 1999-2016 annual PM2.5 department exposure. EEA public monitor exports are source/type compatible, but a reproducible rerun needs a documented monitor-to-department and multi-year aggregation adapter; no OpenAQ query used. https://discomap.eea.europa.eu/map/fme/AirQualityExport.htm

title: Association between exposure to air pollutants and hospitalization for SARS-Cov-2: an ecological time-series study.
outcome_retrieval_evidence: SIH/SUS has a no-login public TabNet query form at https://tabnet.datasus.gov.br/cgi/deftohtm.exe?sih/cnv/niSP.def; it returns public tabulations, but daily B34.2 extraction for the three municipalities needs a query/export adapter.
outcome_variable_evidence: Outcome is daily SIH/SUS hospitalizations with ICD-10 B34.2, with admission date, sex, age, length of stay, discharge/death, and costs reported.
date_key_evidence: Study period is 1 April 2020-31 March 2021 and hospitalization date is explicitly used for daily counts.
geography_key_evidence: Outcome unit is residents of Taubate, Tremembe, and Pindamonhangaba, Sao Paulo; municipal IBGE/SIH geography is required.
covariate_evidence: Primary negative-binomial model includes daily PM2.5, NO2, O3, temperature, relative humidity, and hospitalization date; article reports no further non-exposure covariates.
analysis_specification_evidence: Article specifies a multipollutant negative-binomial model, 95% CI, lags 0-7, RR=exp(coefficient), and stated concentration increments.
aeris_exposure_evidence: CETESB supplies daily ambient pollutant concentrations, compatible in source type with public monitoring data; independent reconstruction requires explicit station/municipality aggregation for the three-city conurbation. https://cetesb.sp.gov.br/ar/qualar/

title: Exposure to air pollution and hospitalization due to COVID-19 in São José dos Campos, Brazil.
outcome_retrieval_evidence: SIH/SUS has a no-login public TabNet query form at https://tabnet.datasus.gov.br/cgi/deftohtm.exe?sih/cnv/niSP.def; a daily B34.2 municipal export is feasible but needs a query/export adapter.
outcome_variable_evidence: Outcome is daily SIH/SUS hospital admissions with ICD-10 B34.2, with admission date and discharge/death fields described.
date_key_evidence: Paper fixes the daily observation window to 1 April 2020-30 April 2021 and uses hospitalization date.
geography_key_evidence: Study location is Sao Jose dos Campos municipality, Sao Paulo; municipality is the outcome/location key.
covariate_evidence: Primary model includes PM10, NO2, O3, temperature, relative humidity, day of week, and calendar day.
analysis_specification_evidence: Paper specifies negative-binomial regression; all pollutants plus temperature/humidity and calendar controls; lag 0-7 estimation; RR transformation; and 10 ug/m3 increment calculation.
aeris_exposure_evidence: CETESB daily monitor data are source/type compatible with public ambient monitoring, but reimplementation needs a documented station assignment/aggregation for Sao Jose dos Campos. https://cetesb.sp.gov.br/ar/qualar/

title: Effects of short- and long-term exposure to atmospheric pollution on COVID-19 risk and fatality: analysis of the first epidemic wave in northern Italy.
outcome_retrieval_evidence: The public repository provides CC-BY-4.0 regional CSV/JSON data. A verified raw CSV endpoint is https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pcm-dpc/COVID-19/master/dati-regioni/dpc-covid19-ita-regioni.csv
outcome_variable_evidence: Primary daily outcomes are regional COVID-19 case and death counts; fatality is deaths divided by same-day cases.
date_key_evidence: Article uses daily reports from 21 February through 19 May 2020.
geography_key_evidence: Two region keys are Lombardy and Veneto, matching the repository's regional records.
covariate_evidence: Primary GEE model includes short-term and eight-year long-term pollutant exposure plus a lockdown indicator; sensitivity models add the most-correlated pollutant or all remaining pollutants.
analysis_specification_evidence: Article gives log-link GEE equations for daily cases/deaths, LOCK dummy, AR(1) working correlation, single/multipollutant sensitivity specifications, and SAS PROC GENMOD.
aeris_exposure_evidence: Article itself identifies EEA hourly/daily monitor data (2013-May 2020) for NO2, O3, PM2.5, PM10, and SO2. This is compatible public monitoring source type, but region-day and eight-year regional mean construction require an aggregation adapter. https://discomap.eea.europa.eu/map/fme/AirQualityExport.htm

title: Cluster of climatic and pollutant characteristics increases admissions for acute myocardial infarction: Analysis of 30,423 patients in the metropolitan area of Sao Paulo.
outcome_source: Brazilian Unified Health System DATASUS hospital information system
outcome_retrieval_evidence: DATASUS SIH/SUS TabNet supports unauthenticated public morbidity queries/downloads: https://datasus.saude.gov.br/informacoes-de-saude-tabnet/
outcome_variable_evidence: Primary outcome is acute myocardial-infarction hospital admissions.
geography_key_evidence: Metropolitan Sao Paulo hospital data require a documented municipality/region aggregation in TabNet.
covariate_evidence: Meteorology and pollutant covariates are described but must be retrieved and aligned from their public source tables.
analysis_specification_evidence: Paper specifies cluster/time-series approach but an adapter is needed to reproduce its cluster construction.
aeris_exposure_evidence: Outdoor criteria-pollutant monitoring exposure is compatible in type; do not require the paper's original exposure model.

title: Spatial proximity to wildfires as a proxy for measuring PM2.5: A novel method for estimating exposures in rural settings.
outcome_retrieval_evidence: BRFSS annual public-use files are downloadable without login: https://www.cdc.gov/brfss/annual_data/annual_data.htm
outcome_variable_evidence: Adult asthma counts must be reconstructed from BRFSS survey responses using the paper's regional definition.
date_key_evidence: Study uses annual wildfire/asthma data; paper reports its study period.
geography_key_evidence: Alaska regional aggregation requires a documented BRFSS geography adapter and Census denominators.
covariate_evidence: Census denominators and wildfire perimeters are public but require source-specific aggregation.
analysis_specification_evidence: Paper bounds the proximity-buffer analysis; reconstructing regional counts and buffers requires an adapter.
aeris_exposure_evidence: Wildfire smoke PM2.5 is AERIS-compatible in source type; evaluation should reconstruct PM2.5 rather than reuse the paper's proximity proxy.
implementation_requirements: Regional BRFSS aggregation and wildfire-geography adapter.

title: An ecological study on the correlation between sanitary vulnerability and air pollution with COVID-19 pandemic burden: What lessons can we learn?
outcome_source: Argentina Ministry of Health COVID database
outcome_retrieval_evidence: Argentina's official catalog provides public COVID case resources without login: https://datos.gob.ar/dataset/salud-covid-19-casos-registrados-republica-argentina
outcome_variable_evidence: Reported outcomes are COVID-19 cases, deaths, and tests used to form pandemic burden measures.
geography_key_evidence: Jurisdiction/locality key must be reconciled to the paper's sanitary-vulnerability geography.
covariate_evidence: SVI and population/confounding inputs need extraction and geographic harmonisation.
analysis_specification_evidence: Ecological correlation/regression is bounded in the paper but requires reconstruction of the reported burden and SVI variables.
aeris_exposure_evidence: Ambient PM2.5 is compatible in type with AERIS public-monitoring reconstruction; geographic aggregation is required.

title: Cancer mortality risk from short-term PM2.5 exposure and temporal variations in Brazil.
outcome_retrieval_evidence: Brazil's public SIM open-data catalogue exposes mortality files without login. The original individual death files are delivered in DATASUS formats and require a documented DBC-to-tabular ingestion adapter before analysis.
outcome_variable_evidence: The paper uses cancer deaths in SIM from 25 ICD-10 cancer sites. Selecting cancer ICD-10 codes and decoding cause-of-death fields from SIM is deterministic but requires a source-format adapter.
date_key_evidence: Each death record carries date of death; the study uses daily observations from 2000-01-01 through 2019-12-31.
geography_key_evidence: Each record includes municipality; the paper aggregates daily PM2.5, temperature, and humidity to municipality and matches cases/controls within municipality.
covariate_evidence: The primary model adjusts for daily mean temperature using a distributed-lag cross-basis, relative humidity, and public-holiday indicator. ERA5 weather and national holiday calendars are public but need extraction and municipality aggregation adapters.
analysis_specification_evidence: The paper gives a bounded primary design: time-stratified case-crossover conditional logistic regression, three-day average PM2.5, matched same-weekday controls in the same month/municipality, temperature cross-basis, relative humidity, and holiday term.
aeris_exposure_evidence: The study exposure is outdoor PM2.5. AERIS-compatible public monitoring records can be assembled by municipality/day, but the paper's original population-weighted modeled 0.25-degree surface cannot be reproduced identically and Brazilian monitor coverage/selection requires an adapter.
implementation_requirements: No source-access blocker found; required outcome and covariate inputs need reproducible source-format and spatial/temporal aggregation adapters.

title: Excess of COVID-19 cases and deaths due to fine particulate matter exposure during the 2020 wildfires in the United States.
outcome_retrieval_evidence: The public repository is directly downloadable without login or a data-use agreement.
outcome_variable_evidence: The repository provides daily county COVID-19 cases and deaths for the 92 wildfire-affected counties.
date_key_evidence: The study period is 15 March through 16 December 2020 with daily records.
geography_key_evidence: County FIPS identifiers support linkage to Census county boundaries.
covariate_evidence: The public package contains the paper's public confounders, including meteorology and mobility; a source-substitution run excludes author PM2.5 and wildfire variables.
analysis_specification_evidence: The paper specifies county-level Bayesian hierarchical zero-inflated negative-binomial distributed-lag models with a 28-day lag.
aeris_exposure_evidence: AERIS can reconstruct county/day ambient PM2.5 from public monitoring data, but the initial OpenAQ-only boundary run returned usable exposure for only 2 of 133 candidate counties.
implementation_requirements: Public data and analysis are fully accessible; retain as a benchmark candidate pending sufficient independently reconstructed exposure coverage.
